care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by getting the first question for the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start with the first important question:

**How old is the child (or children) you're claiming for?**

To properly assess your eligibility, I need to know which age category they fall into:
- **Under 16 years old**
- **16-19 years old**
- **20 years old or over**

Could you tell me the age(s) of the child/children you're asking about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 9 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. Your son Alex is 9 years old, which means he falls into the **under 16 category** and is a qualifying child for Child Benefit purposes.

Let me continue with the next check in the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

This is generally straightforward for a 9-year-old, but I need to confirm for the assessment: Is Alex in any paid employment, or is he in full-time education only (like school)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's just in school like any normal 9-year-old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! That's what we'd expect for a 9-year-old. Alex is not working, so he meets this requirement.

Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right?**

Specifically, is he not receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit

For a 9-year-old, this is typically "yes" - children this young wouldn't normally have these benefits in their own name. Can you confirm that Alex is not receiving either of these benefits?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Alex doesn't receive any of those benefits in his own name. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

For a 9-year-old, the answer should be straightforward - he's not likely to be in an apprenticeship. Can you confirm that Alex is not in any type of apprenticeship programme?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's definitely not in an apprenticeship - he's only 9!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's exactly what I'd expect. Alex is not in any apprenticeship, so he meets this requirement as well. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Now let's check your residency requirements:**

To claim Child Benefit, you need to meet UK residency requirements. There are several ways you could qualify:

**The main ways are:**

1. **Normally live in the UK** - This is the most common route
2. **Have settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. **Have pre-settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme and meet additional criteria (such as working, actively seeking work, having sufficient resources, studying, or being a family member of an EEA/Swiss national)
4. **Crown servant** - Living abroad as a Crown servant in certain qualifying countries

**Which of these applies to you?**
- Are you normally resident in the UK, or
- Do you have settled/pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or
- Are you a Crown servant living abroad?

Or to keep it simple: **Do you normally live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK. I'm currently living abroad.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. You're living abroad. Let me get more details to understand your situation better, as there are still several ways you might qualify for Child Benefit even while living abroad.

**Can you tell me:**

1. **Are you a Crown servant living abroad?** (For example, working for the UK government, Foreign Office, or in certain qualifying countries as a UK representative)

2. **If not, do you have any status under the EU Settlement Scheme?** Specifically:
   - Do you have **settled status**, or
   - Do you have **pre-settled status**?

3. **Alternatively, is there any connection to the UK that might apply** - such as working for a UK employer, or having been sent abroad by a UK employer?

This information will help me determine if you meet the residency requirements for Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of those apply to me. I'm just living abroad - I'm not a Crown servant, I don't have settled or pre-settled status, and I don't work for a UK employer.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Based on what you've told me, it appears you don't meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit eligibility.

The residency requirement states that you must normally live in the UK or meet one of the special circumstances (such as being a Crown servant abroad, having settled/pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or working for a UK employer). Since none of these apply to your situation, unfortunately you would not be eligible for Child Benefit.

Let me provide you with the formal outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Now let me provide you with your final eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Final Outcome: **INELIGIBLE**

**Why you're not eligible:**

You do not meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit. Although your son **Alex** would otherwise qualify as a child for Child Benefit purposes (he's 9 years old and meets all the relevant checks), the fundamental requirement is that the **claimant must normally live in the UK**.

**The residency requirement allows for exceptions only in these circumstances:**
- You have **settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme
- You have **pre-settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme and meet qualifying criteria (working, studying, having sufficient resources, or being a family member of an EEA/Swiss national)
- You are a **Crown servant** living abroad in certain qualifying countries
- You are working for a UK employer abroad (in certain circumstances)

Since none of these apply to your situation, unfortunately you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit.

**What you can do:**
- If your circumstances change and you move back to the UK, you could reapply at that point
- If you believe you might have settled or pre-settled status that wasn't initially apparent, you could explore that option further with HMRC
- For more information, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

I understand this may not be the outcome you were hoping for. If you have any questions about this decision or believe your circumstances are different, you can contact HMRC directly for further advice.
